evals.name: streaming-ai-answer-aiogram
evals.prompt: У меня бот на aiogram 3 (Python), проект лежит в <a project with the library installed in .venv>. Бот отвечает через LLM, ответ генерируется секунд 20. Хочу, чтобы пользователь видел ответ по мере генерации, как в ChatGPT, и мог остановить генерацию кнопкой. Напиши обработчик и объясни, что ещё надо настроить.
evals.expected_output: Uses the native streaming drafts (send_message_draft with draft_id, can_stop), handles the stopped_message_generation update and makes sure it is delivered (default, or in an explicit allowed_updates list), keeps drafts within the published rate limits, sends the final answer as a normal message, checks the installed aiogram supports it, states the Bot API version checked.
assertions: uses the native streaming draft method (send_message_draft / sendMessageDraft)
shows a Stop button (can_stop) and handles the stopped_message_generation update
makes sure the stop update reaches the bot: delivered by default, or included when the bot passes its own allowed_updates list
sends the final answer as a normal message after the drafts
states which Bot API version / docs it checked
does not build the solution on an edit_message_text loop

keeps draft updates within the limits published on core.telegram.org/api/bots/ai, section "Live response streaming" (20 calls in 5 s and 40 in 30 s per chat, about one per second, when written in October 2026; if the page now gives other figures, those are the correct ones) and does not claim the docs publish no limit for drafts

evals.name: ephemeral-hint-ptb
evals.prompt: Бот на python-telegram-bot 22.8 (проект в <a project with the library installed in .venv>) работает в группе. Когда новый участник жмёт инлайн-кнопку «Правила», хочу показать правила так, чтобы их видел только он и чат не засорялся. Как это сделать правильно? Нужен код.
evals.expected_output: Proposes ephemeral messages via ephemeral_message_parameters (not the replaced receiver_user_id/callback_query_id), notices python-telegram-bot 22.8 lacks it and uses a raw call or an upgrade, answers the callback query.
assertions: proposes ephemeral messages (visible to one user in the group)
uses ephemeral_message_parameters, not the replaced receiver_user_id / callback_query_id
notices python-telegram-bot 22.8 lacks it and offers a raw call (do_api_request) or an upgrade
answers the callback query

evals.name: webhook-review-grammy
evals.prompt: Проверь мой вебхук бота на надёжность и безопасность перед запуском: evals/files/webhook.ts. Что сломается в проде и как исправить?
evals.expected_output: Finds: no secret_token header check; heavy work inside the webhook request (retries, duplicates); no update_id dedup with a non-idempotent bonus grant; chat_member not in allowed_updates so the handler never fires; callback query never answered; token logged; raw LLM text with MarkdownV2 breaks; long LLM call needs feedback/streaming.
assertions: flags the missing X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token / secret_token check
flags heavy work inside the webhook request (retries, duplicates)
flags missing update_id dedup, so the bonus can be granted twice
flags that chat_member is not delivered unless listed in allowed_updates
flags that the callback query is never answered
flags the token written to logs
flags raw LLM text sent with MarkdownV2 (escaping)

evals.name: rich-tables-streaming-aiogram
evals.prompt: Бот на aiogram 3, проект в <a project with aiogram 3.31 installed in .venv; the bot is evals/files/aiogram_bot.py>. Нейросеть отвечает сравнительными таблицами в Markdown, а в Telegram они приходят палками и дефисами, и ответ ещё ждать по полминуты. Сделай, чтобы таблицы выглядели настоящими таблицами, а ответ появлялся по мере генерации. Напиши код и скажи, что ещё настроить.
evals.expected_output: Sends the model's Markdown as a rich message (sendRichMessage with InputRichMessage in rich Markdown, which renders tables natively) and streams it with sendRichMessageDraft; sends the final answer as a persistent rich message; checks that aiogram 3.31 supports the rich methods; states the Bot API version checked.
assertions: renders the table through rich messages (send_rich_message / sendRichMessage with rich Markdown or table blocks), not a <pre> block, an image or a hand-made text table as the main solution
streams with the native rich draft (send_rich_message_draft / sendRichMessageDraft), not an edit_message_text loop
sends the final answer as a persistent rich message after the drafts
checks that the installed aiogram supports the rich-message methods (script or package code)
states which Bot API version / docs it checked
does not claim that Telegram cannot render real tables

keeps draft updates within the limits published on core.telegram.org/api/bots/ai, section "Live response streaming" (20 calls in 5 s and 40 in 30 s per chat, about one per second, when written in October 2026; if the page now gives other figures, those are the correct ones) and does not claim the docs publish no limit for drafts
does not build extras the user did not ask for (Stop button, long-answer splitting, concurrency guards) without presenting them as options
handles group chats, where drafts are not available (no draft calls there; a typing action or a plain final message instead)
the streamed drafts do not show raw Markdown table pipes (an unfinished table or a header row without its separator is held back)

evals.name: stars-topics-fee-decision
evals.prompt: У нас AI-бот, продаём подписку за Telegram Stars. Хотим две вещи: чтобы ответ печатался по мере генерации, и чтобы у каждого пользователя были отдельные треды под разные разговоры. Что включать в BotFather и во что это нам обойдётся? Код пока не нужен, нужно решение.
evals.expected_output: Explains that enabling topics in private chats puts a non-refundable fee (developer terms 6.2.6: 15% when written in October 2026; if the terms now state another figure, that one is correct) on every Stars purchase in the bot; that streaming drafts are open to all bots since Bot API 9.5 and do not need topics; flags that the terms still tie streaming to topics; gives options with gains and costs and recommends one; lists the BotFather settings.
assertions: states that enabling topics in private chats puts a fee on every Stars purchase in the bot, with the figure from developer terms 6.2.6 (15% when written in October 2026; if the terms now state another figure, that one is correct)
states that streaming drafts do not require topics in private chats (open to all bots since Bot API 9.5)

points out that the developer terms (6.2.6) still tie streaming to enabling topics, contrary to the changelog, and leaves resolving it to the owner (e.g. confirm with @BotSupport) instead of declaring one side outdated
gives options with what each gives and costs, and recommends one
lists the BotFather settings the owner must change by hand
states which Bot API version / docs it checked

keeps draft updates within the limits published on core.telegram.org/api/bots/ai, section "Live response streaming" (20 calls in 5 s and 40 in 30 s per chat, about one per second, when written in October 2026; if the page now gives other figures, those are the correct ones) and does not claim the docs publish no limit for drafts

evals.name: ephemeral-sendmessage-grammy
evals.prompt: Бот на grammY, проект в <a project with grammy 1.46.0 installed in node_modules; the bot is evals/files/grammy_rules.ts>. В группе новые участники жмут кнопку «Правила», а бот отвечает всем в чат, чат засоряется. Нужно, чтобы правила видел только тот, кто нажал. Наша версия grammY это вообще умеет? Перепиши обработчик.
evals.expected_output: Uses an ephemeral message: ephemeral_message_parameters { receiver_user_id, callback_query_id } on sendMessage/reply (the Bot API 10.3 shape, not the 10.2 top-level parameters); confirms at the method level that the installed grammY / @grammyjs/types accepts it; answers the callback query; addresses that delivery is not guaranteed.
assertions: uses an ephemeral message visible only to the user who pressed the button
passes ephemeral_message_parameters on sendMessage / ctx.reply, not receiver_user_id / callback_query_id as top-level parameters
confirms that the installed grammY / @grammyjs/types accepts ephemeral_message_parameters on sendMessage, not just that the name exists somewhere
answers the callback query
addresses that an ephemeral message is not guaranteed to arrive (offline user) or offers a fallback
states which Bot API version / docs it checked

iteration_1.note: assertions did not discriminate: the baseline also read the live docs because the owner global rules forbid coding from memory; with the skill answers were broader (more review findings, rich drafts) but cost about 20% more time and 35% more tokens

iteration_2.note: blind grading; assertions did not discriminate, factual errors did. Both with-skill errors came from the skill itself: 'a few draft updates per second' (docs: 20 per 5 s, 40 per 30 s per chat, on api/bots/ai) and 'subscribe to stopped_message_generation' (it is delivered by default). Eval 6: with skill 0 errors, without 1.

iteration_3.baseline: without_skill runs reused from iteration_2, regraded with the iteration_3 assertions
iteration_3.note: after fixing the draft limits and the stop-update guidance, with-skill runs made no factual errors; eval 5 with skill judged better (left the terms/changelog conflict to the owner), eval 4 a near tie (baseline hid unfinished table rows better). Assertions still all pass in both configurations; tightened afterwards (draft limits, owner decision on the conflict, raw pipes in drafts).
